### Session 037d0f81-d10c-4973-9bff-6d6c8b04288d - 2026-08-01T16:48:37.536Z

- User (Spencer) asked about Jobber time windows: whether jobs need realistic start/end times to display accurate arrival windows to customers, as opposed to the current 3-hour windows that make customers think the visit will take 3 hours.

- Claude Code checked the live Jobber account and identified three independent fields: job `startAt`/`endAt` (internal calendar block, currently 7 AM–7 PM on most), `arrivalWindow.durationInMinutes` (what customer sees, set to 180 min on 774 of 825 August visits), and `centeredOnStartTime` (false, so window runs *from* the visit start).

- Found a larger defect: because 268 of 518 visits in the next 7 days still have placeholder 7 AM–7 PM times, customers are being told "7:00–10:00 AM" arrivals even when the technician reaches them at 3 PM — not a wording problem, but incorrect time windows.

- Discovered 36–56 timed visits Aug 9+ have *no* arrival window at all; Monday sweep only reaches 14 days out, leaving gaps.

- Identified that `drift-check.mjs` uses the 12-hour visit-width as a sentinel to detect floating vs. pinned visits, so shrinking to 15 minutes would break route automation.

- Recommended three changes: (1) push OptimoRoute's real per-stop times into Jobber as a D-1 routine pass (OptimoRoute already computes them), (2) fix template copy to clarify arrival window ≠ visit duration, (3) close gaps in window coverage.

- Offered to build the D-1 arrival-time sync and draft template rewrite, with canary-test on one day before deploying to cron.
